# Northstar — Monday Business Review: Analysis & Decision Support

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**The October headline revenue is not real growth.** The month looks ~+10–12% up on September, but this is driven almost entirely by two accounting artifacts that will not repeat:

- **Gringotts' annual prepay:** a single invoice of **€120,000** covering **12 months** (INV-2026-10-0236), booked at full value in October. Gringotts normally pays €10,000/month (it paid exactly that in September).
- **A duplicated invoice:** `INV-2026-10-0209` (soylent, €19,500) is loaded **twice** — once from `stripe` and once from `billing_sync`. It must be counted once.

- September total revenue: **€797,100**
- October total, all rows as loaded: **€892,900**
- After removing the duplicate (−€19,500) and normalising Gringotts to its monthly equivalent (−€120,000, +€10,000): **€763,400**
- **Comparable month-on-month: −4.2% (€763,400 vs €797,100)**

The decline is **entirely professional services** (€51,000 → €5,700). Underlying **subscription revenue was roughly flat, up +1.6%** (€746,100 → €757,700).

**Genuine health signals — both buried under the noise:**
- **5 churns in October**, all late in the month: nakatomi (Mid-market/Pro, €180k ARR) plus four SMB Starter accounts (slate-rock, mega-lo-mart, dinoco, buy-n-large, €123.6k ARR combined).
- **Every churned account showed a large usage decline beforehand** (−16% to −37%), and **soylent is currently on that same trajectory** (−27% requests, a revenue downgrade, and a critical API-error ticket).
- **Acme's 45% request drop is not a problem** — it is the expected batch-migration effect (see §2); tokens only fell 12%.

**Decisions supported by the data:**
1. **Segment:** the only defensible cut is **SMB (Starter-led)** — highest churn and thinnest margin — but it is small (~5% of ARR), so treat it as a plan-level fix, not a strategic retreat.
2. **Acquisition:** **No.** Increasing spend on a channel is **not supported** — channel CAC/payback cannot be computed (no spend data exists in the pack), and paid_search's credited revenue is inflated by questionable expansion attribution.
3. **Plan focus:** **Enterprise** — it is ~87% of subscription revenue and 79% of total margin, yet it has the **lowest and falling margin** and contains the largest account-level risks.

---

## 2. REVENUE & CUSTOMER HEALTH — what is really driving the headline

### 2a. Revenue bridge (September → October)

| Item | Sept | Oct (as loaded) | Oct (corrected) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Subscription invoices | 746,100 | 867,700 | 757,700 |
| Professional services | 51,000 | 5,700 | 5,700 |
| **Total** | **797,100** | **892,900** | **763,400** |

Corrections: −€19,500 duplicate; Gringotts annual €120,000 replaced with €10,000 monthly equivalent (its `arr_eur` is €120,000 ⇒ €10k/month).

Result: **−4.2% comparable**. The fall is professional services ($51,000 → $5,700, only one small PS invoice in October). Subscription is essentially flat/marginally up.

**Confirmation that `plans.csv` uses monthly-equivalent billing:** Enterprise plan October revenue = €659,500, which exactly equals the sum of its 14 customers' *monthly* subscription values (Gringotts counted at €10,000). Pro (€66,200) and Starter (€32,000) reconcile the same way. This validates the normalisation above.

### 2b. What is actually changing in subscriptions (+€11,600 net)

- New Starter/Pro logos: spacely +€3,200, cogswell +€2,100, bishop +€1,700, gekko +€2,200, paper-street +€1,900 = **+€11,100**
- Hooli expansion: €18,000 → €21,000 = **+€3,000**
- Soylent contraction: €22,000 → €19,500 = **−€2,500**

**Forward-looking caution:** the churned accounts (nakatomi €15,000 + four SMB ≈ €10,300) are **still billed in October** because they churned mid-month. October's recurring base therefore overstates the live run-rate by roughly **€25,300**; November recurring will drop unless replaced.

### 2c. Acme is a false alarm — do not misinterpret it

| Acme | Requests | Tokens (m) | Tokens/request |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sept | 4,200,000 | 4,620 | 1.10 |
| Oct | 2,310,000 | 4,066 | 1.76 |

Requests fell **−45%** (exactly the migration's estimated 40–50% band) but **tokens only fell −12%**, and tokens-per-request rose from 1.10 to 1.76. This is the signature of a workload moving from many interactive calls to few large batch runs — **the volume is still there**. Acme support tickets also *fell* (4 → 3). Rating Acme as a churn/growth risk would be wrong.

### 2d. The real health problem: usage decline precedes churn

| Account | Oct usage change | Status |
|---|---|---|
| buy-n-large | −37.0% | churned |
| mega-lo-mart | −37.1% | churned |
| dinoco | −35.5% | churned |
| slate-rock | −34.7% | churned |
| **soylent** | **−27.0%** | **active — downgraded, critical ticket** |
| nakatomi | −16.1% | churned |
| acme | −45.0% | active — **explained by migration** |

**Soylent is the standout live risk:** usage −27%, revenue contracted −2.5%, **8 tickets in October (Sept: 3) including a critical `api_errors` ticket**, and several still open/pending. This single €234k-ARR mid-market account is displaying the same pre-churn pattern as the four that left.

Ticket volume overall rose **59 → 74 (+25%)** month-on-month.

---

## 3. ACQUISITION — what can and cannot be concluded

### 3a. Headline channel efficiency (lead → paid trial, same month)

| Channel | Sept leads | Sept trials | Sept rate | Oct leads | Oct trials | Oct rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| paid_search | 520 | 44 | 8.5% | 900 | 58 | **6.4%** |
| content | 260 | 31 | 11.9% | 330 | 34 | 10.3% |
| partner | 60 | 15 | **25.0%** | 75 | 17 | **22.7%** |
| outbound | 160 | 10 | 6.3% | 195 | 11 | 5.6% |

**Partner converts leads to trials ~3–4× more efficiently than any other channel**, but on the smallest volume. Paid_search has by far the most leads but the **lowest conversion and it is falling** (8.5% → 6.4%). Outbound is also weak (≈6%).

### 3b. Acquisition table — new logo vs expansion split

| | Sept | Oct |
|---|---|---|
| New-logo attributed revenue | 246,000 | 133,200 |
| Expansion attributed revenue | 36,000 | **216,000** |
| **Total** | 282,000 | 349,200 |

**In October, 62% of "attributed revenue" is expansions of existing customers, not new business.** Worse, €174,000 of the €216,000 is credited to **paid_search** on campaigns that started **2026-09-28** — from customers that have existed for years (stark 2023, umbrella 2024, globex 2024). Attributing those expansions to a two-week-old campaign is not credible. **Paid_search's apparent revenue surge is an attribution artifact.**

On **new logos only**, the picture is flat-to-down: Sept €246,000 → Oct €133,200, split across content (2 logos), paid_search (2), outbound (1), partner (0 in October).

### 3c. What cannot be concluded

- **CAC payback by channel cannot be calculated at all.** The pack contains **no channel spend data**. This should be stated plainly to the CFO — the requested number does not exist in the current data.
- The funnel's "conversions" are **paid trials in the same month**, not customers, and "**trial-to-paid conversion runs on a longer cycle and is not tracked in this pack**." No channel's true customer yield or payback is derivable.
- Partner's Oct trial surge (17) has **no corresponding Oct acquisition rows** — consistent with a conversion lag, so no conclusion about partner *outcomes* yet.

---

## 4. PLAN ECONOMICS — after cost, not just revenue

| Plan | Month | Revenue | Infra | Support | Total cost | Margin | Margin % | Support % of rev |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enterprise | Sep | 659,000 | 288,000 | 159,000 | 447,000 | 212,000 | **32.2%** | 24.1% |
| Enterprise | Oct | 659,500 | 296,800 | 168,000 | 464,800 | **194,700** | **29.5%** | **25.5%** |
| Pro | Sep | 63,000 | 13,600 | 6,900 | 20,500 | 42,500 | 67.5% | 11.0% |
| Pro | Oct | 66,200 | 16,100 | 8,600 | 24,700 | **41,500** | **62.7%** | 13.0% |
| Starter | Sep | 24,100 | 8,400 | 7,300 | 15,700 | 8,400 | 34.9% | 30.3% |
| Starter | Oct | 32,000 | 11,400 | 10,300 | 21,700 | **10,300** | **32.2%** | **32.2%** |

**What this says:**

- **Pro is the strongest plan by a wide margin** (≈63% margin, ~24% infra intensity) — and it is the smallest. It is the best candidate for *growth investment*, not rescue.
- **Enterprise is where nearly all the money is** (€659,500 revenue, €194,700 margin = **79% of total margin**), but it has the **lowest margin % of any plan, and it is deteriorating** (32.2% → 29.5%). Costs rose ~€17,800 on flat revenue. Enterprise infra is ~45% of revenue and support ~25.5%.
- **Starter is structurally thin** (~32% margin), has the **highest support intensity of any plan (32.2% of revenue)**, and holds all four October SMB churns. It is barely profitable per customer (≈€2,462 revenue vs ≈€1,670 fully-loaded cost per customer/month).
- Note the Enterprise-plan population is **mixed**: 8 Enterprise-segment accounts *plus* 6 Mid-market accounts (Gringotts, soylent, hooli, massive-dynamic, tyrell, duff). The margin erosion and much of the ticket load come from this mid-market tail — **soylent alone generated 8 October tickets**. So "Enterprise plan margin erosion" is partly a *segmentation* issue, not pure scale inefficiency.

---

## 5. RECOMMENDATIONS

**1. Segment decision — do NOT cut a whole segment; fix SMB Starter economics.**
The only deterioration the data supports is in **SMB**, concentrated in **Starter**: all four SMB churns, the highest support-intensity of any plan, and the lowest ARR per customer (≈€34k). However, SMB is only **~€479k of active ARR (~5% of the base)**, and it is still adding logos (5 in October), so a blanket "stop investing in SMB" would save little and forfeit a self-replacing funnel. Recommendation: **tighten the Starter plan's support/unit economics and set a retention gate**, and verify retention before any deeper cut. **Do not touch Enterprise or Mid-market investment** — they are 94% of ARR.

**2. Acquisition decision — do NOT increase channel spend on this data.**
There is **no spend data**, so CAC and payback are incalculable; and paid_search's credited revenue is inflated by implausible expansion attribution. The one efficiency signal (partner's ~23–25% lead-to-trial rate) is on the smallest budget and has no matched October outcomes. Recommendation: **hold spend**, obtain per-channel spend, and treat paid_search attribution as unverified. Before scaling anything, re-run attribution excluding expansions and re-baseline paid_search.

**3. Plan decision — Enterprise deserves next quarter's attention (with Pro as the scale bet).**
Enterprise is 79% of margin and is losing margin (29.5%, falling) while carrying the biggest account risks (soylent, Acme migration). Focus engineering on **reliability and support-cost drivers** in the Enterprise plan (API errors/performance — the categories driving tickets and churn risk). Separately, **Pro has the best unit economics (≈63%)** and is the natural target for growth investment once acquisition economics are validated.

**4. Operational follow-ups (from the data):**
- Data/BI: deduplicate `INV-2026-10-0209` and fix the `billing_sync` load; adopt monthly-equivalent reporting for annual prepays so October does not repeat this distortion.
- Account management: escalate **soylent** now (usage −27%, downgrade, critical + open tickets) — it matches the pre-churn profile of every account lost this month.

---

## 6. UNCERTAINTIES / DATA ISSUES

**Confirmed data defects**
- **Duplicate invoice:** `INV-2026-10-0209` (soylent, €19,500) appears under **both** `stripe` and `billing_sync`. Counted twice in any raw total.
- **Billing-timing distortion:** Gringotts' €120,000 annual invoice is recorded at full value in October (`billing_period_months = 12`), inflating the month by €110,000 vs its true €10,000 monthly value.
- **Reporting mismatch:** `revenue.csv` (invoice-date basis) and `plans.csv` (monthly-equivalent MRR) give different October totals; leadership must not read the invoice-dated number as MRR.

**Metrics that cannot be computed reliably**
- **CAC and CAC payback by channel — impossible.** No spend data in the pack. Any payback figure would be fabricated.
- **Channel conversion-to-customer, and trial-to-paid** — not derivable: funnel "conversions" are same-month **paid trials**, and trial-to-paid is explicitly not tracked.
- **True acquisition ROI** — compromised by expansion bookings being credited to channels (€216,000 of €349,200 in October), most implausibly to paid_search.

**Unsupported causal claims to avoid**
- "October revenue grew ~10%" — false once the one-off annual and duplicate are removed (underlying −4.2%).
- "Acme is churning/declining" — the drop is the documented batch migration; tokens held up.
- "Paid_search is our best channel" — its credited revenue is expansion-driven and attribution is implausible.
- "SMB is collapsing" — SMB lost 4 logos but added 5; the pattern is high churn with offsetting acquisition, not decline.

**Preserved uncertainty**
- Five churns landing in one month (four on Starter) *may* indicate a plan, pricing, or product issue, but the pack contains **no churn reasons** — this remains a hypothesis, not a finding.
- The professional-services drop (€51k → €5.7k) may be lumpiness rather than a trend; two data points cannot establish direction.
- Mid-market lost the single largest churn (nakatomi, €180k) yet also contributes expansions — its net direction is genuinely unclear from this pack.
